children: Taiwan's September exports likely rose 46.5% from a year earlier, according to a Wall Street Journal poll of five economists. That would be stronger than August's 41% and July's 32.9%. Although the chip powerhouse likely maintained strong exports momentum last month, some economists caution that there are signs of slowing artificial-intelligence exports growth. The relentless rise in AI hardware, which has driven the gain in Asian export values, is easing too. Meanwhile, DBS economists caution that the global AI boom is facing rising headwinds from tighter monetary policies led by the Federal Reserve, higher bond yields and rising financing costs. (sherry.qin@wsj.com)
